persona.name: Lauren Lindqvist

occupation.title: Pediatric Nurse (RN)
occupation.description: Twelve-hour shifts on a pediatric medical-surgical floor: meds, charting, scared parents, constant handwashing. Sanitizer and nitrile gloves rule her skin's life more than any product does.

persona.education: BSN from the University of Minnesota.
long_term_goals: Move to the NICU within two years
Buy a small house near the lakes with her fiancé
Keep her eczema controlled enough that handwashing doesn't hurt
persona.style: Calm, kind, and clinically literal — she explains things the way she explains discharge instructions to parents: plainly, with the 'why' attached. Skeptical of trends because she's seen what damaged skin barriers actually look like. Scrubs, fleece, no makeup most days; everything she uses must be fragrance-free or her skin announces it within hours.

likes: Thick hand cream that survives glove changes
Drugstore brands her derm actually endorses
dislikes: Being upsold at counters when she asks for 'gentle'

beliefs: The skin barrier is medical, not cosmetic
Boring and consistent beats exciting and new

general: Repurchases the same ceramide cream in the 16oz tub
Applies hand cream at every charting break
Asks her dermatologist before changing anything
Reads 'for sensitive skin' labels with open suspicion

morning: Lukewarm rinse, ceramide cream, mineral SPF if she'll see daylight
evening: Gentle cleanser, prescription hydrocortisone on flare spots, thick cream
weekend: Meal prep, one cabin weekend a month in summer

health.physical: Chronic atopic dermatitis on hands and eyelids, flares every winter; otherwise healthy.
health.mental: Compassion fatigue she manages with strict work-life boundaries.

relationships.name: Erik
relationships.description: A carpenter; he installed a humidifier in every room the winter her eczema got bad.

relationships.name: Dr. Patel
relationships.description: The only person whose product advice she takes without a second opinion.
